$comment: Cross-SDK catalog for the engine-owned media artifact store (ADR 017): ranged reads, disposal, the limits, and what the engine discards on its own. Like streaming/engine-conformance.json it is a scenario catalog: 'setup' is normative prose naming the fakes and what they write, 'expect' is shared data, and each SDK registers one handler per 'id' behind a guard test that fails when the handler ids and the ids here differ. Cases run run() unless 'mode' is 'stream'. A provider's 'finished' artifacts are the references its writer's finish() returned, in order; 'finishedReadable' says whether readArtifact still finds each one after the run. Cases with a destinationRef run on a host whose artifact-destination service accepts every reference and records each write, unless the setup says the host has none or its write fails.

$expectKeys.output: Fields of the result's (or, in stream mode, the terminal's) output.artifact, compared exactly; the id is checked only for being present.
$expectKeys.reads: readArtifact calls made in order after the run, each with its request and the chunk's offset, byte length, totalBytes and done. Every chunk's bytes must equal the pattern over [offset, offset + length).
$expectKeys.readRejects: readArtifact calls that must throw, with the error class, retryable flag, details.code, or a validation issue path.
$expectKeys.runRejectsWith: run() threw: the error class and, when given, details.code.
$expectKeys.providerCallCounts: How many times each provider was entered.
$expectKeys.providerObservedCodes: details.code of every error each fake's writer threw at it, in order.
$expectKeys.finishedReadable: Per provider, whether each artifact it finished is still readable after the run.
$expectKeys.terminal: Stream mode: fields of the terminal payload; 'absentOutput' asserts the key is missing.
$expectKeys.maxSerializedEventBytes: Stream mode: the largest JSON encoding of any delivered StreamEvent, in bytes, must stay below this.
$expectKeys.rejectsBeforeRouting: run() threw before any provider was entered: the error class and details.code.
$expectKeys.destinationWrites: What the host's artifact-destination service was asked to write, in order: the destinationRef, the artifact's media type and byte length, and whether the bytes follow the pattern.

cases.description: A finished artifact is read whole in one call, with the metadata the engine recorded.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` starts the artifact with durationMs 500, writes 1000 bytes in one write, finishes, and returns the artifact. The consumer reads with no offset or maxBytes.

cases.description: Ranged reads that follow each chunk's end cover every byte exactly once and report the last chunk as done.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` writes 1000 bytes in three writes (300, 300, 400), finishes and returns the artifact. The consumer reads with maxBytes 400 at offsets 0, 400 and 800.

cases.description: No read returns more than the engine's maximum read size, whatever the caller asks for.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. The engine is configured with maxReadBytes 256. `p1` writes 1000 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact. The consumer reads with no maxBytes, then with offset 900 and maxBytes 5000.

cases.description: Reading the same range twice returns the same bytes; a read does not consume the artifact.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` writes 1000 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact. The consumer reads offset 100 with maxBytes 50 twice.

cases.description: An offset at the end returns an empty, final chunk; one past the end is a validation error.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` writes 1000 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact. The consumer reads at offset 1000, then at offset 1001.

cases.description: Disposing twice is harmless, and a disposed artifact can no longer be read.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` writes 10 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact. The consumer disposes it twice, then reads it.

cases.description: An id the engine never issued reads like a disposed one.
cases.setup: No run. The consumer reads artifactId 'art_unknown'.

cases.description: Handing over an artifact commits the run: a failure after it is the run's failure, no fallback happens, and the engine discards the artifact the application never received.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` writes 10 bytes, finishes, then throws Unavailable. `p2` is registered as the fallback and would return a 10-byte artifact.

cases.description: An artifact that exceeds the per-artifact limit fails its attempt before commit, so the run falls back.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. The engine is configured with maxArtifactBytes 100. `p1` writes 101 bytes in one write and rethrows what the writer throws. `p2` writes 50 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact.

cases.description: The store refuses a handoff that would exceed its total limit, before commit; disposing an earlier artifact makes room again.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. The engine is configured with maxStoreBytes 150. `p1` writes 100 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact, rethrowing anything the writer throws. The consumer runs three times, disposing the first run's artifact between the second and third runs.

cases.description: An artifact a winning attempt finished but did not return is discarded; the returned one stays.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` finishes a 10-byte artifact, then a 20-byte one, and returns the second.

cases.description: An artifact output this attempt did not hand over -- a forged or stale id -- is a provider fault; nothing was committed, so the run falls back.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. `p1` returns an artifact output with id 'art_forged', mediaType 'audio/wav', owner 'engine', lifetime 'until_disposed', without writing anything. `p2` writes 10 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact.

cases.description: Cancelling a stream after the artifact was handed over but before the result ends the run as cancelled, with no output, and discards the artifact.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` writes 10 bytes, finishes, then waits for cancellation. The consumer cancels once the artifact has been handed over.

cases.description: A stream that produces a large artifact delivers only small events: the bytes stay in the store and the terminal carries a reference.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251, continuing across writes of one artifact. `p1` writes 1048576 bytes, finishes, and emits result with the artifact.

cases.description: A host with no artifact-destination service refuses a request that names a destination before any provider runs, rather than producing media with nowhere to go.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'] and destinationRef 'dest_greeting', privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251. The host has no artifact-destination service. `p1` would write 10 bytes, finish and return the artifact.

cases.description: The engine writes the finished artifact to the application destination, returns it as application-owned, and keeps no copy.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'] and destinationRef 'dest_greeting', privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251. `p1` writes 1000 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact.

cases.description: A failed destination write happens after commit, so the run fails without falling back, and the engine discards its copy.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'] and destinationRef 'dest_greeting', privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251. The host's write fails. `p1` writes 10 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact; `p2` is registered as the fallback and would do the same.

cases.description: The engine checks the media type the store recorded when the artifact was written, not the one the provider claims when it returns the reference: an audio/mpeg artifact relabelled audio/wav does not satisfy a request for audio/wav. Handing it over had committed the run, so the mismatch is terminal and the artifact is discarded.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'], privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251. `p1` writes 10 bytes as 'audio/mpeg', finishes, and returns that artifact's reference with mediaType changed to 'audio/wav'. `p2` is registered as the fallback and would return a 10-byte 'audio/wav' artifact.

cases.description: A cancel that lands while the host is writing the artifact to its destination ends the stream cancelled, not completed. The engine does not interrupt a write already in progress, so the cancelled terminal carries the application-owned artifact: its bytes are at the destination, and the application owns them.
cases.setup: Request: text_to_speech, speech 'Hallo' in de-AT, artifact delivery with mediaTypes ['audio/wav'] and destinationRef 'dest_greeting', privacy local_required. Every fake declares a text_to_speech capability with artifact output 'audio/wav'. Written bytes follow the pattern byte[i] = i % 251. The host's write blocks until the test releases it. `p1` writes 10 bytes, finishes and returns the artifact. The consumer cancels once the host write has started, then releases the write.
